'''Donavan Deante McKinney''' (born June 16, 1992)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Donavan McKinney |url=https://www.gongwer.com/directories/bio.cfm?nameid=400401 |access-date= |website=Gongwer News Service-Michigan}}</ref> is an American politician serving as a member of the [[Michigan House of Representatives]] since 2023, currently representing the [[Michigan's 11th House of Representatives district|11th district]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.legislature.mi.gov/publications/CitizensGuide.pdf |title=Michigan Citizen's Guide to State Government, 2025–2026, 103rd Legislature |publisher=Michigan Legislature |year=2025 |location=Lansing, Michigan |language=en}}</ref> A member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] and the [[Democratic Socialists of America]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Why Both Republicans and Democrats Are Worried About the DSA |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |language=en-US |date=August 3, 2026 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ilmDQo1o9kM |access-date=August 3, 2026}}</ref> McKinney is the member-elect for [[Michigan's 13th congressional district]] in [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Michigan#District 13|2026]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=McNamara |first=Russ |date=2025-09-24 |title=Detroit Black political leaders rally behind Donavan McKinney |url=https://wdet.org/2025/09/24/detroit-black-political-leaders-rally-behind-donavan-mckinney/ |access-date=2025-11-06 |website=[[WDET]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Early life==
McKinney was born and raised on the northeast side of Detroit near Seven Mile Road and Van Dyke Avenue and attended [[Renaissance High School (Michigan)|Renaissance High School]].<ref>{{Cite podcast|url=https://detroit-is-different.pinecast.co/episode/39386cdf/a-community-first-vision-for-congress-donavan-mckinney|host= Khary Frazier|date= June 19, 2025|title=A Community-First Vision for Congress Donavan McKinney|work= Detroit is Different|access-date=2025-07-16}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Lawrence |first1=Eric D. |title=Mallory McMorrow: Legislators who don't work on transit needs should be voted out |url=https://freep.com/story/news/local/michigan/detroit/2024/01/31/mcmorrow-irwin-state-of-transit-2024-detroit/72401836007/ |access-date=21 March 2026 |publisher= |date=31 January 2024|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]}}</ref> He relied on public transportation to get to school, spending five hours every day on the bus.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Barrett |first1=Malachi |title=Lawmakers tell Detroiters: 'Get more intense' on public transit demands |url=https://www.bridgedetroit.com/lawmakers-tell-detroiters-get-more-intense-on-public-transit-demands/ |access-date=22 March 2026 |publisher=[[Bridge Detroit]] |date=31 January 2024}}</ref> He was mostly raised by his grandmother while his mother worked.<ref name="macomb">{{cite news |last1=Hotts |first1=Mitch |title=Two native Detroiters make history as Macomb County's first Black state lawmakers |url=https://www.macombdaily.com/2022/12/04/two-native-detroiters-make-history-as-macomb-countys-first-black-state-lawmakers/ |access-date=22 March 2026 |publisher=[[Macomb Daily]] |date=4 December 2022}}</ref> His family moved 13 times while he was growing up, mostly due to evictions.<ref name="prospect">{{cite news |last1=Janssen |first1=Emma |title=The Squad Could Have a New Member in 2026 |url=https://prospect.org/2025/04/28/2025-04-28-squad-member-2026-justice-democrats-donavan-mckinney-michigan/ |access-date=22 March 2026 |publisher=[[American Prospect]] |date=28 April 2025}}</ref>

McKinney earned a [[bachelor's degree]] in [[public policy]] from the [[University of Michigan]] in 2014.

==Early career==
McKinney worked as a legislative director in the [[Michigan Legislature]], and then later in community engagement for the nonprofit Community Development Advocates of Detroit, before becoming an organizer for healthcare in the Michigan [[Service Employees International Union]].<ref name="macomb" /><ref name="itt">{{cite news |last1=Day |first1=Eli |title=The Next Fight in the Democratic Party |url=https://inthesetimes.com/article/donavan-mckinney-2026-congress-justice-democrats |access-date=23 March 2026 |publisher=[[In These Times (magazine)|In These Times]] |date=5 June 2025}}</ref> In 2020, [[Governor of Michigan|Governor]] [[Gretchen Whitmer]] appointed him to her Environmental Justice Council where he helped develop the pandemic plan to restore sewage service and water to Detroit residents via the $2&nbsp;million Water Restart Grant Program and her statewide Water Reconnection Executive Order.<ref name="macomb" /><ref>{{cite news |last1=Nann Burke |first1=Melissa |title=Detroit lawmaker Donavan McKinney jumps into race to unseat Shri Thanedar in Congress |url=https://detroitnews.com/story/news/politics/2025/04/28/state-rep-donavan-mckinney-challenging-detroit-shri-thanedar-for-congress-seat-michigan/83318824007/ |access-date=23 March 2026 |issue=28 April 2025 |publisher=[[Detroit News]]}}</ref>

==Political career==
===Michigan House of Representatives===
McKinney was elected to the [[Michigan House of Representatives]] from the [[Michigan's 14th House of Representatives district|14th district]] in the [[2022 Michigan House of Representatives election|2022 election]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Meet Rep. McKinney |url=https://housedems.com/donavan-mckinney/about/ |access-date=2023-11-21 |website=housedems.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="mich-2022-general-results">{{cite web |title=2022 Michigan Election Results - General |url=https://mielections.us/election/results/2022GEN_CENR.html |publisher=[[Michigan Secretary of State]] |access-date=November 29, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221129162327/https://mielections.us/election/results/2022GEN_CENR.html |archive-date=November 29, 2022 |date=November 28, 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Following court-mandated redistricting of the Detroit area,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hendrickson |first1=Clara |title=Court orders metro Detroit legislative maps redrawn |url=https://www.freep.com/story/news/politics/2023/12/21/court-orders-redraw-of-detroit-area-legislative-districts/71382879007/ |access-date=January 3, 2025 |work=[[Detroit Free Press]]}}</ref> McKinney ran in the [[Michigan's 11th House of Representatives district|11th district]] for the [[2024 Michigan House of Representatives election|2024 election]], winning re-election.<ref name="mich-2024-general-results">{{cite web|title=2024 Michigan Election Results|url=https://mvic.sos.state.mi.us/votehistory/Index?type=C&electionDate=11-5-2024|publisher=[[Michigan Secretary of State]]|access-date=November 24, 2024|date=November 22, 2024|url-status=live|archive-date=November 24, 2024|archive-url=https://archive.today/20241124174348/https://mvic.sos.state.mi.us/votehistory/Index?type=C&electionDate=11-5-2024}}</ref>

McKinney has been critical of Michigan's utility companies, and of corporate influence in politics in general. He co-sponsored a bipartisan bill package that would prohibit political campaign contributions from utility companies, such as [[DTE Energy]] and [[Consumers Energy]], as well as from major state government contractors, such as [[Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan|Blue Cross Blue Shield]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Davidson |first=Kyle |date=2025-04-25 |title=Lawmakers resurrect legislation to end political spending from utilities and government contractors  |url=https://michiganadvance.com/2025/04/25/lawmakers-resurrect-legislation-to-end-political-spending-from-utilities-and-government-contractors/ |access-date=2025-07-06 |website=Michigan Advance |language=en-US}}</ref> McKinney also supports an increase to the credit that Michigan energy companies must pay to consumers affected by prolonged power outages, arguing that the current rate of $35 per day is not enough to offset the costs of spoiled medicine or groceries.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Davidson |first=Kyle |date=2023-08-28 |title=Thousands remain without power following severe storms and tornadoes across Michigan |url=https://michiganadvance.com/2023/08/28/thousands-remain-without-power-following-severe-storms-and-tornadoes-across-michigan/ |access-date=2025-07-06 |website=Michigan Advance |language=en-US}}</ref>

McKinney was one of two primary sponsors on legislation in 2023 that would create the position of medication aide in nursing homes to fill the gap between entry-level nursing assistants and licensed practical nurses and help address severe staff shortages by freeing up licensed practical and registered nurses to do more patient care. Governor Whitmer signed the bipartisan bill into law.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Erb |first1=Robin |title=A new kind of worker in Michigan nursing homes could address staff shortage |url=https://bridgemi.com/michigan-health-watch/new-kind-worker-michigan-nursing-homes-could-address-staff-shortage/ |access-date=22 March 2026 |publisher=[[Bridge Michigan]] |date=3 December 2023}}</ref>

In November 2023, McKinney joined two dozen other lawmakers, including State House Majority Leader [[Abraham Aiyash]], in sending a letter to President [[Joe Biden]] to urge him to advance "a lasting ceasefire" in the [[Gaza war]]. The letter urged "the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, the adherence of all international laws, and aid to ensure that every person living in [[Israel]], [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]], and the [[West Bank]] can live with [[self-determination]], dignity and humanity."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rahal |first1=Sarah |title=25 Michigan lawmakers urge Biden to 'advance a lasting ceasefire' |url=https://detroitnews.com/story/news/local/michigan/2023/11/23/25-michigan-lawmakers-urge-biden-to-advance-a-lasting-ceasefire/71689057007/ |access-date=22 March 2026 |publisher=[[Detroit News]] |date=23 November 2023}}</ref>

In 2024, McKinney introduced legislation that would protect the privacy of individuals who filed complaints of misconduct against police officers. He also introduced legislation that would require separation records to include any disciplinary actions or investigations against an officer, and to require the [[Michigan Commission on Law Enforcement Standards]] to revoke an officer's license if they use excessive force that results in the death or serious bodily injury of another individual.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Anthony |first1=Sarah |title=Michigan Legislators Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Improve Public Safety and Community Trust With Police |date=November 22, 2024 |url=https://senatedems.com/anthony/2024/11/22/michigan-legislators-introduce-bipartisan-legislation-to-improve-public-safety-and-community-trust-with-police/ |publisher=State Senator [[Sarah Anthony]] |access-date=23 March 2026}}</ref> Neither of these bills became law.

Major successes in the district include helping to win over $10&nbsp;million in community violence intervention programs, which led to the creation of the statewide community violence intervention initiative to focus on preventing gun violence. McKinney also won $600&nbsp;million in federal funds to [[Lead abatement in the United States|replace lead pipes]] in Detroit and surrounding suburbs.<ref name="prospect" />

===2026 Congressional campaign===
{{further|2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Michigan#District 13}}
In April 2025, McKinney announced his candidacy for [[Michigan's 13th congressional district]], a notoriously impoverished section of the state<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lanard |first=Noah |date=August 5, 2026 |title=Michigan's Primary Reckoning for the Democrats |url=https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2026/08/michigans-primary-reckoning-for-the-democrats-donavan-mckinney-will-lawrence-abdul-el-sayed/}}</ref> in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Michigan|2026 election]], challenging incumbent [[Shri Thanedar]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wethington |first=Paula |date=April 28, 2025 |title=Donavan McKinney announces run for Congress, seeking to oust Shri Thanedar |url=http://cbsnews.com/detroit/news/donavan-mckinney-announces-run-for-congress/ |access-date=April 28, 2025 |website=CBS News}}</ref> He is endorsed by U.S. Rep. [[Rashida Tlaib]], former U.S. Rep. [[Brenda Lawrence]], the [[Justice Democrats]], Senator [[Bernie Sanders]],<ref name=":1" /> the [[Working Families Party]], the Metro Detroit chapter of the [[Democratic Socialists of America]], more than a dozen state legislators, and the Michigan chapter of [[Service Employees International Union]], of which McKinney is a former member and organizer.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spangler |first=Todd |title=Rep. Rashida Tlaib endorses Donavan McKinney in Democratic race against Shri Thanedar |url=https://www.freep.com/story/news/politics/elections/2025/05/12/rashida-tlaib-endorsement-thanedar-donavan-mckinney/83573454007/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250512135523/https://www.freep.com/story/news/politics/elections/2025/05/12/rashida-tlaib-endorsement-thanedar-donavan-mckinney/83573454007/ |archive-date=2025-05-12 |access-date=2025-07-06 |website=Detroit Free Press}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wu |first=Nicholas |date=April 28, 2025 |title=Justice Democrats launch new primary challenge |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/04/28/justice-democrats-launch-new-primary-challenge-00309380 |access-date=April 28, 2025 |website=Politico}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last = Gans|first = Jared|title = Sanders backs progressive challenger to Thanedar|url = https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5353430-bernie-sanders-michigan-endorses-donavan-mckinney/|website = [[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]|date = 2025-06-17|access-date = 2025-06-17}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Neavling |first=Steve |title=Major union endorses Donavan McKinney for Congress in growing wave of progressive support |url=https://www.metrotimes.com/news/major-union-endorses-donavan-mckinney-for-congress-in-growing-wave-of-progressive-support-39764501 |access-date=2025-07-06 |website=Detroit Metro Times |date=June 23, 2025 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Snyder |first1=Branden |title=Working Families Party Endorses Donavan McKinney, William Lawrence, Rep. Rashida Tlaib in Michigan Congressional Races |url=https://workingfamilies.org/2026/02/wfp-endorses-donavan-mckinney-william-lawrence-rep-rashida-tlaib-in-michigan/ |access-date=23 March 2026 |publisher=[[Working Families Party]] |date=27 February 2026}}</ref><ref name="itt"/>

McKinney has said his campaign will focus on lowering costs, especially car insurance and child care.<ref name="wdet">
{{cite news |last1=McNamara |first1=Russ |title=Detroit Black political leaders rally behind Donavan McKinney |url=https://wdet.org/2025/09/24/detroit-black-political-leaders-rally-behind-donavan-mckinney/ |access-date=22 March 2026 |publisher=[[WDET]] |date=24 September 2025}}</ref> He would like to abolish ICE.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Arshad |first=Minnah |date=June 16, 2026 |title=Bernie Sanders-backed challenger takes on Thanedar in 13th District race |url=https://www.bridgedetroit.com/bernie-sanders-backed-challenger-takes-on-thanedar-in-13th-district-race/}}</ref> He stated "There's like .0001%, like very small percentage of folks, poor people, take advantage of the system," <ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Elkind |first=Elizabeth |date=August 3, 2026 |title=Socialist House candidate says he agrees with Republicans on 'one issue' |website=[[Fox News]] |url=https://www.foxnews.com/politics/socialist-house-candidate-says-he-agrees-republicans-one-issue}}</ref>

On August 4, McKinney defeated Thanedar.<ref>{{cite news |last=Kamisar |first=Ben |title=Democratic Rep. Shri Thanedar loses his primary to a progressive challenger in Michigan
|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/democratic-rep-shri-thanedar-loses-primary-progressive-challenger-mich-rcna590894 |work=[[NBC News]] |date=August 5, 2026 |access-date=August 5, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
McKinney and his wife Shaunté Wilcher, an attorney,<ref name="macomb" /> have three children. The oldest was born in 2022 and the youngest in 2025.<ref>{{Cite Instagram |user=donavanmckinney |postid=CZ9VP68l5lH |title=Good morning, I want to thank GOD and my wife Shaunté Wilcher for giving me the best gift this Valentine's Day, and that is the gift of fatherhood! Introducing the newest addition to the family, our little sonshine Donavan Emmanuel McKinney II. Can't believe he's already 3 weeks old. Want to acknowledge all the parents out there and those who came before us. Parenting, as well as taking care of any human being no matter how old, is hard work and should be celebrated. Truly blessed and honored to be a husband and father. Love my wife and son to infinity. Happy Valentine's Day 💙 Photo Credit: Ashleigh Davis Photography |date=14 February 2022}}</ref> He has said that even with his statehouse salary that is twice the median income in his district, he and his wife can still only afford to put their oldest child into childcare.<ref name="wdet" /> McKinney developed [[asthma]] as a child.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Groz |first=Zachary |date=2026-07-29 |title=The CBC Challenge in Detroit |url=https://prospect.org/2026/07/29/shri-thanedar-donavan-mckinney-congressional-black-congress-detroit-michigan/ |access-date=2026-07-29 |website=The American Prospect |language=en-US}}</ref>
